extracted.intended_audience: heads of executive departments, agency procurement and contracting officials, contracting officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for agency decisionmakers and contracting offices on applying OMB Circular A-76 to determine whether commercial/industrial-type work should be performed in-house or contracted out, and how to conduct and document cost comparisons, justifications, and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary policy precepts
rubrics_metrics.description: This policy builds on three equally valid policy precepts: (a) Rely on the Private Sector; (b) Retain Certain Governmental Functions In-House; (c) Aim for Economy; Cost Comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use private sector sources when available; retain inherently governmental functions in-house; when private performance is feasible use rigorous comparative cost analysis to decide between contract and in-house performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on the Private Sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Where private sources are available, they should be looked to first to provide commercial or industrial goods and services needed by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should not compete with private enterprise for commercial/industrial-type work unless other Circular provisions justify in-house performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain inherently governmental functions in-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain functions are inherently governmental in nature and must be performed in-house by Government personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include discretionary application of Government authority (investigations, prosecutions, direction of armed services, foreign relations), monetary transactions and entitlements (benefit programs, tax collection), and in-house core R&D/testing capabilities needed for technical analysis and evaluation. Requirements beyond a justified 'core capability' are not governmental functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for economy via comparative cost analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: When private performance is feasible and no overriding factors require in-house performance, rigorous comparison of contract costs versus in-house costs should be used to decide how the work will be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative cost analyses must conform to this Circular and the Cost Comparison Handbook and be the principal basis for economy-based decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Government commercial or industrial activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity operated and managed by a Federal executive agency which provides a product or service that could be obtained from a private source; must be separable and regularly needed, not a one-time short duration project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An activity should be identifiable with an organization or type of work and meet both separability and recurring operational need criteria before applying Circular procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification thresholds: expansion, new start, conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'expansion' involves additional capital investment of $100,000+ or increasing annual operating costs by $200,000+ provided increases exceed 20%; an expansion increasing capital or operating cost by 100%+ is a 'new start'; a 'conversion' transfers work from Government activity to private contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these numeric thresholds and percentage tests to classify proposals and determine applicability of Circular procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of private commercial source
rubrics_metrics.description: A private business, university, or other non-Federal activity, located in the United States (including territories, DC, Puerto Rico), which provides the required commercial or industrial product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only such domestic non-Federal entities count as private commercial sources for purposes of determining availability and conducting competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and exceptions to application
rubrics_metrics.description: No executive agency will engage in or contract for commercial/industrial activities except in accordance with this Circular. The Circular does not provide authority to enter into contracts, will not be used to create employer-employee relationships with contractors, and will not be used to justify contracting solely to meet personnel ceilings or avoid salary limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major system acquisitions are governed by A-109; consulting services of purely advisory nature and certain printing/binding exceptions apply; do not apply the Circular where contrary to law or treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of products/services from other Federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess property and services available from other Federal agencies should be used in preference to new starts or contracts unless private sector procurement is more economical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formal programs (e.g., ADP sharing) exist, reported excess capacity can be used without further justification. Absent such programs, use of another agency's activity must be justified per paragraph 8. Agencies should not expand capacity merely to serve other agencies and must notify users if support will be terminated when capacity is needed for their own requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization when no satisfactory commercial source available
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government activity can be authorized without comparative cost analysis when (a) there is no private commercial source capable of providing the needed product/service, or (b) use of a private source would cause unacceptable delay or disruption of an essential agency program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must make all reasonable efforts to identify sources: place at least three notices in the Commerce Business Daily over 90 days (or two notices over 30 days for urgent requirements), seek assistance from GSA/SBA/DOC. Conclusions that private sources are unsatisfactory or would cause unacceptable delay must be specifically documented in cost, time, and performance terms. Classified program status, mission importance, possibility of strike, or urgency alone are insufficient justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: National defense justification for in-house operation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government activity operated by military personnel may be justified when (a) personnel used are deployed/subject to deployment in direct combat support, (b) activity is essential for training in skills exclusively military, or (c) activity provides appropriate work assignments for career progression/rotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depot/intermediate maintenance may be justified under criteria approved by the Secretary of Defense, limiting in-house capability to the minimum necessary. Such justifications require detailed explanations and high-level approval (assistant secretary level or equivalent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization when Government higher cost not a bar
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government activity may be authorized if a comparative cost analysis indicates the Government can provide the product or service at a lower total cost than private sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy-based authorizations require a properly conducted comparative cost analysis per the Circular and Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison common ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons must be based on the same scope of work and level of performance; require a precise work statement with monitorable performance standards; use standard cost factors prescribed by the Cost Comparison Handbook; aim at full cost including overhead and indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must defend any cost variations between cases. Solicitations for continuing workloads should include prepriced or renewal options to guard against 'buy-in' pricing. Ordinarily, do not conduct cost comparison studies for activities < $100,000 annual operating costs unless special circumstances (inadequate competition or unreasonable commercial prices) justify it. Use 10% per annum as opportunity cost for capital investments and sale proceeds as prescribed in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating contract costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract cost figures must be based on a binding firm bid or proposal solicited per acquisition regulations; bidders must be told an in-house cost estimate is being developed and that a contract may or may not result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include 4% of contract price or expected cost as the Government's cost factor for administering contracts, in addition to other contract-use costs specified in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating costs of Government operation (standard cost factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government cost calculations should ensure operations are organized/staffed for efficient performance and use prescribed cost factors: retirement benefits factor 20.496, insurance (life and health) 3.7%, workmen's compensation/bonuses/unemployment 1.9%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should precede reviews with internal management reviews/reorganizations to improve efficiency where feasible. Use these standard factors unless agency supplements are justified and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion savings threshold for existing in-house activities
rubrics_metrics.description: An existing in-house activity will not be converted to contract performance on the basis of economy unless it will result in savings of at least 10% of the estimated Government personnel costs for the period of the comparative analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use estimated Government personnel costs over the analysis period as the baseline for the 10% savings test.

rubrics_metrics.name: New start approval savings threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new start' will not be approved on the basis of economy unless it will result in savings compared to contract performance at least equal to 10% of Government personnel costs, plus 25% of the cost of ownership of equipment and facilities, for the period of the comparative analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both personnel savings (10%) and an ownership cost component (25% of equipment/facilities cost) when evaluating new starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review of cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: All cost comparisons must be reviewed by an activity independent of the cost analysis preparation to ensure conformance with the Cost Comparison Handbook instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish an independent review activity to verify methodology and adherence to handbook rules before final decisions are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency implementation and administrative responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must designate an official at assistant secretary or equivalent level and subordinate contact points to have overall responsibility for implementing this Circular; establish central offices to maintain cognizance of implementation actions and have access to decision documents and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 90 days agencies must promulgate the Circular with minimum internal instructions identifying designated officials and forward copies to OMB’s OFPP for review. Central offices must respond timely to requests concerning inventories, schedules, reviews, and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract requirements when conversions result
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts awarded as a result of reviews under Circular A-76 must (a) contain applicable clauses related to equal employment opportunities, veterans' preference, minimum wages and fringe benefits including OFPP Policy Letter No. 78-2 on 'wage busting'; (b) include a provision giving displaced Federal employees the right of first refusal for qualified positions on the contract; (c) be awarded to responsible and responsive bidders; and (d) be administered and monitored to achieve proper performance using appropriate contractual remedies when performance is unsatisfactory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clauses and post-employment conflict-of-interest standards are included, follow acquisition regulations for responsibility/responsiveness, and actively monitor contractor performance with remedies for deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations to displaced Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must exert maximum effort to find suitable employment for displaced Federal employees, including priority consideration for Government positions, paying reasonable training and relocation costs, arranging gradual transition during conversions, and coordinating with the Department of Labor and other agencies to obtain private sector employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement placement, training, relocation, and transition measures to mitigate adverse employment impacts from conversions and to facilitate placement in Government or private sector jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-owned, contractor-operated (GOCO) activities treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive review of GOCO activities is necessary to determine applicability of the Circular; in the interim the Circular is to be applied only to new starts and expansions of Government-owned equipment and facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not uniformly apply Circular to existing GOCOs until comprehensive review completes; apply to new starts/expansions as interim measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to R&D activities and core capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies with a need for in-house R&D capability can consider a 'core capability' in R&D as a governmental function; additional guidance will be developed to determine and justify core capability size and application of the Circular to R&D requirements. Periodic review of inventoried R&D activities is deferred for one year except for new starts/expansions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interagency committee (OFPP and OSTP) will study R&D implementation issues and recommend uniform guidelines; until supplemental guidance is issued, defer comprehensive application for inventoried R&D activities for one year, except for new starts and expansions.
